title: Manually load a kernel module
summary: If a driver or feature is not working, you might need to manually load its kernel module. This is done using the modprobe command.

steps.explain: Use sudo modprobe followed by the module name to load it into the kernel.

placeholders.name: MODULE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the kernel module to load.

rollback.explain: To unload the module, use rmmod or modprobe -r.

placeholders.name: MODULE_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the kernel module to unload.

warnings: Loading incorrect modules can cause system instability.
If you upgraded your kernel but did not reboot, modprobe may fail silently.
